newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion closes down on weak world trends.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion closes down on weak world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees lower at 4,680 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,700 rupees amid sluggish physical buying and weak trend in the world market.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) settled 300 rupees lower at 54,700 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,000 rupees. They were down by 300 rupees per piece on Tuesday.

** Silver (.999) closed 90 rupees lower at 7,300 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,390 rupees on the back of fresh arrivals while setback in the world market prompted profit-taking. Silver was up by 45 rupees per kg on Tuesday.

Gold 24 carat closed 20 rupees lower at 4,680 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,700 rupees amid lower than expected seasonal buying while losses in the world market dragged local prices downward, dealer said.
Gold was down by 30 rupees per 10 gramme on Tuesday. Arrivals of imported gold werer low but sentiment was quiet at the close amid limited activity.
Meanwhile prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 300 rupees lower at 54,700 rupees each against the previous close of 55,000 rupees. They were down 300 each on Tuesday.

Silver (.999) closed 90 rupees lower at 7,300 rupees per kg down against the previous close of 7,390 rupees as fresh arrivals prompted profit-taking at the improved level while a setback in the world market and slow industrial buying capped the rally. Silver was up by 45 rupees per kg on Tuesday.

"Overall market sentiment was subdued at the close of the session amid expectation that the government may further liberalise the import policy for precious metals in the upcoming exim policy," said M. L. Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Exchange.
"Even licence premium of special licence to import precious metals has also dropped again from 13.50/14 percent to 11.30 percent today," he added. (Conversion $1=35.88 rupees)
